Credit prepaid or bring-your-own-hardware orders as revenue and the rest as options; read a residual-value guarantee as the lender's doubt.
Hold gross margin against the stated target before crediting the ramp: Perma-Pipe's 30% in December is the line to clear.

Nvidia's days sales outstanding give back the 14 days Eisman counted, or its terms for investment-grade customers return to 90 days.
Perma-Pipe converts $57 million or more at a gross margin above 30% while Lumentum and Coherent report their ramps at target margin.

call.stance: The price has left the model
call.line: A frontier model no longer commands a price per token for long. The lab still does, and only a prospectus says what that price is worth.
actions: Separate token volume from token dollars: OpenRouter's 57% to 67% and Vercel's 62% in September are volume; the dollar share is uncounted.
Date every run-rate before comparing two: Longriver's May, Romero's July and Kim's October 2 figures are not updates of one another.
Read the customer note before the growth rate when the prospectus lands: Silverio's quarter from two customers is the line to clear first.
flips: A prospectus with audited revenue near the relayed run-rates, no customer above a tenth of sales and no investor-linked revenue to disclose.
Alphabet sizes the TPU contracts with Anthropic inside them on October 28 and Cloud growth holds without them, retiring Burry's charge.
No registration on EDGAR by October 31 while either lab cuts list prices again; the house moves toward the open-weights reading.

call.line: Data centers pay for their own wires. The higher capacity price their demand sets lands first on every PJM household's bill.
actions: Compare medians, not states: PJM's nine rose a median 11.7% per kilowatt-hour in the year to July, against 5.6% elsewhere.
Separate the wire from the scarcity: pledges fund the upgrades a project triggers; the capacity price reaches every PJM bill.
Mark December 9: PJM's auction for 2029/2030 shows whether the price ceiling still binds.
flips: The median gap between PJM's nine and the other 42 falls below four points in the federal data for 2026.
A rule makes large loads bring their own capacity, and PJM's December 9 auction clears below the price ceiling.
Texas household prices rise as fast as PJM's in the 2026 data, putting the cause in the fuel and wires both grids share.
call.side: The bill no state can shield

parts.headline: The Cash Arrives Unevenly
parts.question: Is AI revenue arriving fast enough for the biggest spenders to pay for their data centers out of their own cash?

call.stance: Only Microsoft pays with room to spare
call.line: Microsoft pays for its build from its own cash. Alphabet and Meta spend most of theirs; Amazon spends more than its operations bring in.
actions: Divide capital spending by operating cash, company by company: in the first half of 2026 Microsoft spent 65.3%, Amazon 137.8%.
Hold free cash flow to one ruler: Meta's own measure gave $784 million for the June quarter of 2026; cash less purchases, $1.7 billion.
Read the financing section beside the spending line: Alphabet sold $49.6 billion of stock in June 2026, and Meta borrowed $24.9 billion.
flips: Alphabet spends under 80 cents of each operating dollar in the September quarter: its cash is catching up with its build.
Microsoft's purchases pass 85% of its operating cash in the September quarter: even the strongest cloud stops paying its way.
The four's purchases top their operating cash for the September quarter or for 2026: the group stops paying, toward the debt side.

questions.question: Can the AI trade survive a 10-year Treasury above 5% and an oil shock at the same time?
questions.headline: Can the AI trade survive a 10-year Treasury above 5% and an oil shock at the same time?

parts.headline: Oil Is the Headline. The Real Yield Is the Bill.
parts.question: Can the AI trade survive a 10-year Treasury above 5% and an oil shock at the same time?

call.stance: The trade pays the real yield
call.line: Oil reaches the AI trade through the Fed and the real yield while inflation expectations stay put. The multiple shrinks; the trade survives.
actions: Split every move in the 10-year into real yield and breakeven: from Feb 27 to Oct 8, 2026, 115 of its 125 basis points were real.
Price long-dated earnings against a 10-year at 5.5%, where Howell's Aug 14 projection put the market multiple below 20 times.
Count AI borrowing as a rates input: Eisman tied about $500 billion of AI debt issuance to the 10-year's climb on Oct 9.
flips: The 10-year closes at 5.50% or higher with breakeven inflation under its May 4 high of 2.50%: the two shocks compound.
The 5-year, 5-year forward rate on FRED closes above 2.60%: the shock has reached inflation expectations.
The Fed holds on October 28 and the real yield closes under 2.50% by December 9: the boom is paying the rate.

call.stance: The seller finances part of the demand
call.line: Nvidia's receivables ran 9% to 16% of sales above its own collection pace by July 26, 2026; five accounts owed 70% of them.
actions: Compute days outstanding yourself on November 18: receivables over the quarter's revenue, times 91. July 26, 2026 gave 59.6.

Free cash flow tops 71% of net income on Nov 18, its average in the four quarters before July: the cash came in and the terms were timing.
AMD or Broadcom reports a gigawatt-scale accelerator deal with no warrant, investment, loan or guarantee by Dec 9: demand pays its own way.
